shops.name: Hashigo Honten
shops.name_jp: 支那麺 はしご 本店
shops.description: A spicy ramen restaurant (tantanmen). It's a popular spot so there may be a wait. It stays open late, so the recommendation is to have drinks in Ginza and finish the night off with this ramen.
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座6-3-5 第二ソワレ・ド・ビル 1F

shops.name: 3chome no Curry yasan
shops.description: A renowned restaurant serving baked cheese beef curry. It gets very crowded during the day, so it is recommended to go right when it opens.
shops.address: 東京都中央区京橋3-9-9 ウィンド京橋ビル B1F

shops.name: Nishimura
shops.description: A long-established tonkatsu restaurant. I once waited in line to get into this place and was approached by an older man behind me, who told me that he had visited tonkatsu restaurants all over the country and this one was the best.
shops.note: May not have English menu and English-speaking staff available.
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座3-12-6 盛重ビル 1F

shops.name: Tonkatsu Tonki Meguro Honten
shops.name_jp: とんかつ とんき 目黒本店
shops.description: A renowned tonkatsu restaurant with a history of nearly 90 years. There is always a line during the day, but turnover is very fast. Their excellent operation is also a must-see: staff ask for your order when you come in, and what you ordered comes out piping hot as soon as you sit down.
shops.reservation: Dinner only, for groups of 4 or more
shops.address: 東京都目黒区下目黒1-1-2

shops.name: Nico Chelsea
shops.description: A stylish French bistro tucked away in a back alley of Kagurazaka. It specializes in game meat (gibier). Which game is available depends on that day's supply, but every dish is excellent. You can pick your own wine from the wine cellar, which makes it fun. It is a very popular restaurant, so reservations are essential.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区津久戸町3-6

shops.name: Kagurazaka Yakitori Tora
shops.name_jp: 神楽坂 焼鳥 虎
shops.description: A yakitori restaurant on the slightly pricier side for Japan (though still only about $80). The yakitori itself is very good, and the all-you-can-drink plan even includes Yamazaki whisky, so it is great value. It has counter seats only, so going in a small group is recommended. Reservations are essential. Its Tabelog rating is low because it is a new restaurant with few reviews.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区神楽坂2-11 AYビル 1F

shops.name: Suisui Nihonbashi Tokyo
shops.name_jp: 純米酒専門 粋酔 日本橋東京店
shops.description: A restaurant where you can drink as much as you like from more than 100 kinds of sake collected from all 47 prefectures of Japan. The range of sake is huge, and if you book a course, you can enjoy it all on an all-you-can-drink basis. The food is decent, so this is a place to go for the sake. Reservations for large groups are also possible.
shops.note: It is unclear how well English is supported.
shops.address: 東京都中央区日本橋3-7-10 タンペイ日本橋ビル B1F

shops.name: Dairen (Chinese Home Cooking)
shops.description: A down-to-earth Chinese restaurant that has long been loved by students and office workers. The pan-fried gyoza are very good. It is definitely not the kind of place that appears in travel magazines, so it is recommended if you want to experience a restaurant where local Japanese people go.
shops.address: 東京都港区芝5-15-3 大連ビル

shops.name: Fractale
shops.description: One of the top rum bars in Japan. It is so famous that when it comes to rum in Tokyo, almost every bartender will name this bar. Besides rum, it also has beer and whisky. An authentic bar with a calm atmosphere. Its Tabelog rating is low because it has few reviews; on Tabelog, bars generally tend to get low ratings.
shops.address: 東京都品川区上大崎2-14-3

shops.name: Antonic Nakameguro
shops.description: A small gin bar along the Meguro River. It is a cozy place with only a few counter seats, but you can enjoy gins from all over the world. Gin is also sold in the basement.
shops.address: 東京都目黒区東山1-9-13 東山鈴房荘103

shops.name: Bondy Jimbocho Honten
shops.name_jp: 欧風カレー ボンディ 神保町本店
shops.description: One of the most famous curry restaurants in Japan, and the pinnacle of Japanese-style curry. Rather than strong spices, it is known for the richness and mellowness that come from slowly simmering apples and onions. To everyone from South Asia: this is curry adapted to Japanese tastes, so please forgive us (lol).
shops.address: 東京都千代田区神田神保町2-3 神田古書センター 2F

shops.name: Shanaiya
shops.name_jp: 薬膳スープカレー・シャナイア
shops.description: A restaurant serving yakuzen (medicinal) curry. Despite the name, there is no medicine in it; it is a spice curry made with plenty of ingredients that help with things like recovering from fatigue. Reservations are possible at dinner, but at lunchtime it uses a numbered-ticket waiting system. You can also join the waiting list online, but everyone applies when it opens at 10:30, so you need to be ready at that time.
shops.address: 東京都目黒区三田1-5-5

shops.name: La Maison Dami
shops.name_jp: ラ メゾン ダミ
shops.description: A small French bistro in Meguro. The food is excellent, and the pâté Reo had here was among the best he has ever eaten in his life.
shops.address: 東京都品川区上大崎3-4-9 SEIWAビル 1F

shops.name: Horumon Masaru
shops.description: A Japanese-style BBQ restaurant. Since you grill offal (organ meat), it may not be very familiar to non-Japanese people, but it is very popular among Japanese people. There is not much regular meat, so it is not really recommended for people who do not like offal.
shops.address: 東京都港区芝5-21-14

shops.name: Ramen Taniseya
shops.description: In Japan there is a genre called Yokohama Iekei ramen, based on a pork-bone and soy sauce broth. There are many famous shops in this genre in places such as Yokohama and Shin-Sugita, and this is a well-regarded one that is easy to reach from central Tokyo. There are many Yokohama Iekei shops in Tokyo, but quality varies a lot, so be careful. When you hand over your meal ticket, you can choose the noodle firmness, the strength of the soup and the amount of fat. Reo likes "soft, strong, less fat," but most people generally choose firm noodles.
shops.address: 東京都港区新橋3-11-1 イーグル烏森ビル 1F

shops.name: Menya Kuro
shops.description: A well-regarded Yokohama Iekei shop in Tokyo. For an explanation of Yokohama Iekei, see the description of Ramen Taniseya.
shops.address: 東京都目黒区目黒1-6-12 ワンエム目黒 1F

shops.name: Shinjuku Yakiniku Gyutan no Lemon (Main Shop)
shops.name_jp: 新宿焼肉 牛たんの檸檬 総本店
shops.description: A shop serving thick-cut beef tongue. Many people may be hesitant to eat beef tongue, but its chewy texture is very popular in Japan. We recommend eating it with rice. There are also sister shops besides this one, so please try whichever is easiest to get to.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区西新宿7-16-12 YSビル B1F

shops.name: Bar Tarrow's
shops.description: An authentic bar in Kagurazaka. It has a very large number of whiskies, and the bartender, who has a wealth of experience and knowledge, serves whisky that suits your taste. We don't know how much English he can speak, but he is a wonderful bartender who, we can say for certain, will serve you attentively while using a translation device or similar. Besides whisky, the cocktails are also delicious, and there is a wide variety of rum and other spirits. You can also smoke cigars.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区神楽坂3-6-29 MIビル 3F

shops.name: Shokushuka Okamiya
shops.description: A traditional Japanese izakaya. It is near the house where Reo used to live, and the seafood is very good. A hidden gem loved by locals.
shops.note: We think they can hardly handle English, so you will need to use translation tools or similar.
shops.address: 東京都江東区富岡1-7-10

shops.name: Ramen Benkei (Monzen-Nakacho)
shops.name_jp: らーめん弁慶 門前仲町店
shops.description: There are two flavors: soy sauce and miso. We recommend soy sauce. It is Japanese junk ramen topped with lots of back fat, and the bowls are quite dirty. But the taste is definitely very addictive. Reo ate so much of this ramen that he gained 5 kg. The main shop is in Asakusa, but he has never been there, so he chose this shop.
shops.address: 東京都江東区深川1-1-8
